here\n\nThe issue is discussed here: https://forum.pkp.sfu.ca/t/ojs3-editing-user-roles-in-multi-journal-installations/28711\n\nThe problem: if a user is registered to more than one journal, the journal manager can not edit the roles the user has in her journal. In OJS2 this was possible and in OJS3 journal managers can still add the reviewer role when doing a review assignment.\n\nSuggestion: \n- allow editing user roles within a given context but do not allow editing the user detail (name etc.). \n- add a new \"edit roles\" feature to the users grid\n- for users that exist in multiple journals, do not show the \"edit\" feature for journal managers (no use if they can not edit anyway)\n\nProblem with legislation: @bozana raised the problem with data privacy and user \"contracts\". Maybe we could just send a notification when journal managers adds a new role for a user. A big shout out to @withanage, @ajnyga, @bozana, @asmecher, @jardakotesovec and John for helping me fine tune the work further and make the process more GDPR compliant.\r\n\r\n**Summary of the requirement**\r\n\r\n1. In the “Users \u0026 Roles” section of the settings, we add a new “Invite user to take a role” action that can be used to invite any user to the journal OJS software based on an email address. The email sent will add the following: \r\n- Invitation request along with details of the role, starting date etc. \r\n- ORCiD verification details\r\n- GDPR compliance\r\n\r\n2. Reviewer can be added to OJS in two ways\r\n- _Through the review section of the submission:_ Here the Journal Manager (JM henceforth) / Editor can click on “Add a reviewer” action and will see the following: Reviewers already associated with the Journal and added to OJS and send a review request to them, “Add a new user”- here the JM/Editor can invite a user via email to not only review the submission but also be an OJS user in reviewer capacity- and “Enroll an existing user” - here the JM/Editor can add the reviewer role to a user who already has other OJS roles along with sending an invitation to review the submission. \r\n- _Through the “Users \u0026 Roles” section:_ Here the JM/Editor can either add a new user to OJS as a reviewer or add a reviewer role to an existing OJS user. The user will then be shown in the existing reviewer section of “Add a reviewer” on a submission. \r\n\r\n3. Multiple hosted Journal OJS Installation: For Multiple Hosted Journals, Editors/ JMs cannot access information of users of one Journal to another. In spite of the journals being hosted on the same OJS instance, the user will have to go through the verification again to protect the information to be GDPR compliant. This is the same method followed by likes of Slack wherein even if the channel is hosted by the same company, the invitation process needs to be followed and accepted by the user. However, I as a user will not have to create a new account, I can use my existing OJS logins and verify and accept the role.\r\n\r\n4. Other important considerations\r\n- Even if the user information is publicly available, the JM / editor cannot input the information without consent. This will be translated in the journey in a way where the editors can input the information but they wont be stored in the system. They are shown to the user as suggestions when they accept the invite and the user approves or changes it. Post which the information is stored in the system\r\n- Co-author reauthorization is required even if the user is an existing OJS user\r\n\r\n5. ORCiD Pre-requisite\r\n- Starting with 3.5.0, ORCiD Verification would not happen through a plugin. We're rewriting ORCiD support to be integrated into OJS rather than maintaining a plugin. The option to make ORCiD mandatory should be present as part of the 3.5.0 implementation; it shouldn't be necessary to write up a plugin to add the \"make ORCiDs mandatory\" checkbox.\r\n- If  the JM/System Administrator/Editor has marked ORCiD verification as mandatory, then the email invitation sent will highlight that the verification is mandatory. If it’s not enabled then the ORCiD mandatory message on the email will not be shown\r\n- Mandatory or not, when the user is redirected to the ORCiD website to verify they have an option to skip the step. Since we cannot customize the ORCiD verification screen to show skip or not, the email will be the vehicle for communication.\r\n\r\n### Below are the user flows for inviting users to a role in OJS\r\n\r\n**A. However, I as a user will not have to create a new account, I can use my existing OJS logins and verify and accept the role**\r\n\r\n1. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/7a4783c0-09d7-4f42-a27f-b4193a0e7967)\r\n\r\n2. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/17f82c92-b76b-4c99-b3a0-c02260a369b2)\r\n\r\n\r\n3. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/97e46350-d20a-4a51-ba63-d89ec0feb834)\r\n\r\n4. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/83c9dcc4-6c08-4a0d-8147-1d586d949342)\r\n\r\n5. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/84f99733-6b31-44f9-bc75-ea959d31e8c6)\r\n\r\nAs you can see the process is similar upto this point because to the editor its inviting a new user to their journal.\r\n\r\n6. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/c6c858f0-8623-4728-87d5-853be5ce6b18)\r\n\r\n7. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/ed18ebc5-95f3-4738-8158-5fc645d494a9)\r\n\r\nAn existing OJS user, has two options here, either to link their existing OJS account or to create a new one using a new email id. Do note that even if the user uses an existing account, no information about the user activity can be shared with other journals in the same installation\r\n\r\n8. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/9efb0744-ab2b-4e9b-a420-4ed7302ad462)\r\n\r\n9. \r\n![image](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/assets/112014397/88d9d528-1b68-4f53-89b2-a69e468d8397)\r\n\r\n\r\n\r\n","bodyHTML":"\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eHello,\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eI made a user flow that reflects the all the research, discussions and feedback received on this issue over the last few years along with some minor testing with a small user group at the Copenhagen Sprint. A big shout out to \u003ca class=\"user-mention notranslate\" data-hovercard-type=\"user\" data-hovercard-url=\"/users/withanage/hovercard\" data-octo-click=\"hovercard-link-click\" data-octo-dimensions=\"link_type:self\" href=\"https://github.com/withanage\"\u003e@withanage\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca class=\"user-mention notranslate\" data-hovercard-type=\"user\" data-hovercard-url=\"/users/ajnyga/hovercard\" data-octo-click=\"hovercard-link-click\" data-octo-dimensions=\"link_type:self\" href=\"https://github.com/ajnyga\"\u003e@ajnyga\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca class=\"user-mention notranslate\" data-hovercard-type=\"user\" data-hovercard-url=\"/users/bozana/hovercard\" data-octo-click=\"hovercard-link-click\" data-octo-dimensions=\"link_type:self\" href=\"https://github.com/bozana\"\u003e@bozana\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca class=\"user-mention notranslate\" data-hovercard-type=\"user\" data-hovercard-url=\"/users/asmecher/hovercard\" data-octo-click=\"hovercard-link-click\" data-octo-dimensions=\"link_type:self\" href=\"https://github.com/asmecher\"\u003e@asmecher\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca class=\"user-mention notranslate\" data-hovercard-type=\"user\" data-hovercard-url=\"/users/jardakotesovec/hovercard\" data-octo-click=\"hovercard-link-click\" data-octo-dimensions=\"link_type:self\" href=\"https://github.com/jardakotesovec\"\u003e@jardakotesovec\u003c/a\u003e and John for helping me fine tune the work further and make the process more GDPR compliant.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSummary of the requirement\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIn the “Users \u0026amp; Roles” section of the settings, we add a new “Invite user to take a role” action that can be used to invite any user to the journal OJS software based on an email address. The email sent will add the following:\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eInvitation request along with details of the role, starting date etc.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eORCiD verification details\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eGDPR compliance\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003col start=\"2\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eReviewer can be added to OJS in two ways\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cem\u003eThrough the review section of the submission:\u003c/em\u003e Here the Journal Manager (JM henceforth) / Editor can click on “Add a reviewer” action and will see the following: Reviewers already associated with the Journal and added to OJS and send a review request to them, “Add a new user”- here the JM/Editor can invite a user via email to not only review the submission but also be an OJS user in reviewer capacity- and “Enroll an existing user” - here the JM/Editor can add the reviewer role to a user who already has other OJS roles along with sending an invitation to review the submission.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cem\u003eThrough the “Users \u0026amp; Roles” section:\u003c/em\u003e Here the JM/Editor can either add a new user to OJS as a reviewer or add a reviewer role to an existing OJS user. The user will then be shown in the existing reviewer section of “Add a reviewer” on a submission.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003col start=\"3\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMultiple hosted Journal OJS Installation: For Multiple Hosted Journals, Editors/ JMs cannot access information of users of one Journal to another. In spite of the journals being hosted on the same OJS instance, the user will have to go through the verification again to protect the information to be GDPR compliant. This is the same method followed by likes of Slack wherein even if the channel is hosted by the same company, the invitation process needs to be followed and accepted by the user. However, I as a user will not have to create a new account, I can use my existing OJS logins and verify and accept the role.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOther important considerations\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEven if the user information is publicly available, the JM / editor cannot input the information without consent. This will be translated in the journey in a way where the editors can input the information but they wont be stored in the system. They are shown to the user as suggestions when they accept the invite and the user approves or changes it. Post which the information is stored in the system\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCo-author reauthorization is required even if the user is an existing OJS user\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003col start=\"5\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eORCiD Pre-requisite\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eStarting with 3.5.0, ORCiD Verification would not happen through a plugin. We're rewriting ORCiD support to be integrated into OJS rather than maintaining a plugin. The option to make ORCiD mandatory should be present as part of the 3.5.0 implementation; it shouldn't be necessary to write up a plugin to add the \"make ORCiDs mandatory\" checkbox.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf  the JM/System Administrator/Editor has marked ORCiD verification as mandatory, then the email invitation sent will highlight that the verification is mandatory. If it’s not enabled then the ORCiD mandatory message on the email will not be shown\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eMandatory or not, when the user is redirected to the ORCiD website to verify they have an option to skip the step. Since we cannot customize the ORCiD verification screen to show skip or not, the email will be the vehicle for communication.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003ch3 dir=\"auto\"\u003eBelow are the user flows for inviting users to a role in OJS\u003c/h3\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA. data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Ok, you are probably correct that better tackle users & roles first, since the reviews is probably more complicated. But I already wrote this longer roundup that includes the review stuff as well.</p>
<p dir="auto">Comments? <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/NateWr/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/NateWr">@NateWr</a> <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/asmecher/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/asmecher">@asmecher</a> <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/jmacgreg/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/jmacgreg">@jmacgreg</a></p>
<h1 dir="auto">Requirements</h1>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Users & Roles. We add a new "Invite user to a role" action that can be used to invite any user on the site based on an email address.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Add reviewer in Review stage. We replace the current "Add a new user" and "Enroll an existing user" actions with a single "Invite a new reviewer" action.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h1 dir="auto">Workflows for editor</h1>
<p dir="auto">1 a. The editor needs to add an new user. The user has no existing roles in the context and the editor can not see her in the list. The editor selects Add new user and fills in the form. The system says that the email is already used => The system shows a link "Invite the user to acquire a role in [contextName]" => New modal window opens showing the users email (not editable) and a selection of roles (checkbox) that the invitation will include. At least one role needs to be selected to send the invitation.</p>
<p dir="auto">1 b. The editor needs to add an new user. The user has some role in the context but the editor does not find her in the list for some reason. The editor selects Add new user and fills in the form. The system says that the email is already used => The system shows a link "Invite the user to acquire a role in [contextName]" => New modal window opens showing the users email (not editable) and a selection of roles (checkbox) that the invitation will include. The roles that the user already has are active but checkboxes are disabled. At least one role needs to be selected to send the invitation.</p>
<p dir="auto">1 c. The editor needs to add a new role to a known user. The user has some role in the context and the editor finds her in the list. There is a new "Invite to acquire a role" action available. => New modal window opens showing the users name and email (not editable) and a selection of roles (checkbox) that the invitation will include. The roles that the user already has are active but checkboxes are disabled. At least one role needs to be selected to send the invitation.</p>
<p dir="auto">1 d. The user has role X in the context, the editor needs to remove role X from that user. What should be done with this? We could of course allow users the <em>deselect</em> editorial roles by themselves from the User Profile? This would be the most GDPR compliant way.</p>
<ol start="2" dir="auto">
<li>The editor tries to send a review request but the selected person is not a reviewer yet or the editor does not find her on the list. We have a new "Invite a reviewer" action that opens an ordinary review request form that has an email field on top. The editor fills in an email address and checks the request details and sends in the request. As long as the reviewer has not reacted, the system will only show the email address in the review assignments grid. (<a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/NateWr/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/NateWr">@NateWr</a>, I know you have been thinking of using hashkeys, but here the editor really needs to see some concrete information about who has been invited, has to be the email I think!)</li>
</ol>
<h1 dir="auto">Workflows for user</h1>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>The user receives an email telling her that she has an existing user account in [siteName] and that she has been offered new roles in [contextName]. The email will then list the offered roles and will include an accept link. By clicking the link, the user will be logged in to the context and the offered roles are attached to her account. The system will give a success message.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">2 a. The invited reviewer does not have an existing user account. She receives a message saying that she has been invited to do a review in [contextName] the review details are in the bottom. The email explains that she first has to create an user account by following the link given in the email. Clicking the link will open a simplified version of the registration form. After filling in the form, an user account is created, the user is logged in and then redirected to the review form step 1. At this point, the editor starts to see the full name of the reviewer in the review assignments grid.<br>
There is also an alternative link for rejecting the request and in this case no user account is ever created.</p>
<p dir="auto">2 b. The invited reviewer has an existing user account but no reviewer role. She receives a message saying that she has been invited to do a review in [contextName] the review details are in the bottom. Clicking the link will open review form step 1 which is now accessible for users without the reviewer role. By accepting the review, a reviewer role is attached to the user.  At this point, the editor starts to see the full name of the reviewer in the review assignments grid. If the user declines, no role is attached.</p>
<p dir="auto">2 c. The user was a reviewer already, but the editor did not find her and used the Invite a new reviewer action. Here the system will figure things out and will send an ordinary review request. The editor will see the user's name right from the beginning.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button data-component="Button" type="button" aria-label="👍 1 reaction" role="switch" aria-checked="false" class="prc-Button-ButtonBase-9n-Xk reactionToggleButton__j2dnln" data-inactive="true" data-loading="false" data-size="small" data-variant="default" aria-describedby="_R_3dae5gutkr85_ _R_3dae5gutkr85H2_"><span data-component="buttonContent" data-align="center" class="prc-Button-ButtonContent-Iohp5"><span data-component="leadingVisual" class="prc-Button-Visual-YNt2F prc-Button-LeadingVisual-UySKu prc-Button-VisualWrap-E4cnq">👍</span><span data-component="text" class="prc-Button-Label-FWkx3"><span class="sr-only" id="_R_3dae5gutkr85_">React with 👍</span>1</span></span></button><span class="sr-only" id="_R_3dae5gutkr85H2_">Reacted by <!-- -->Jakov M. data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">I was wondering how this change could affect a JM workflow and I have two points to draw attention at first moment regarding when a user is invited.</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">If an JM invites a user who was already invited, OJS should let the JM knows that that email address is already invited rather than only in use. This message should cover the time gap from the invitation till confirmation by the user.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">When an user rejects the invitation, will the JM be able to invite again without any system warning? Because a user might be no willing to join the journal, and different JMs might be not aware of it and invite him over and over again till the user send an email complaining about it.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">On that note, could a user have an option such like:</p>
<ul class="contains-task-list">
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Incomplete task">  I <strong>do</strong> want to join (accepts the invite)</li>
<li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Incomplete task">  I <strong>don't</strong> wan join now (doesn't accept the invite but would like to join  in the future maybe. He/she would like to join on the next 6 months/ day / weeks or any other time frame )</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">It could add some extra work, but I was wondering how to improve the experience of being invited going further than just <em>yes</em> or <em>no</em> to the invitation.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">I think the scenario where a user rejects but is invited again mostly applies to review requests. The other case where you usually need the invite feature is when you add new editorial members and the invite process there is more a formality: the new editorial member probably already knows she will be invited before receiving a message.</p>
<p dir="auto">Now that we are not creating a full user account before the user accepts the review request, I do not know if it is a good idea to limit the amount of requests/invitations. Two reason:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">If a person says no to a request concerning submission A, it does not mean she wants say no to submission B. <strong>The decisions the user is making is not about creating an user account. It is a decision whether she wants to review this submission and that can depend on many things.</strong><br>
(I think already now editors are sending review requests for persons who have rejected before. Probably it is even more common than with this new feature, because with the current code after the first request the system has created an user account and a reviewer role so the user is visible in the reviewers list against her will.)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">We also have to take multijournal installations into account. If a person says "no" to Journal A, it does not mean she wants to say "no" to Journal B as well.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr>
<p dir="auto">Partly related to this question is what happens after the rejection of a review request. The only data we have stored is the email. Can we keep on showing that in the rejected review request?</p>
<p dir="auto">If we decide that it is personal data which we <strong>can not</strong> store without consent, then what do we do with it? Do we only present it as "Review request #24356" and delete the email? And if we do that, how do we prevent the editor from requesting the same reviewer again on that same submission? Or do we maybe delete the email after the review stage is ready? Do the editors have an obligation to store the email for archiving purposes? Or is it enough that they store the names of the reviewers who accepted and did the actual review?</p>
<p dir="auto">If we decide that we <strong>can</strong> store the email without consent when the request is declined, then the user might create an user account by herself later. Do we in that case attach the stored review request to the user account that she creates? Remember that the solution described above is based on the idea of creating a "proto user account" that uses the <code class="notranslate">users</code> table but only stores the email when the invite is created.</p>
<p dir="auto">I am maybe more inclined to delete the email and the "proto account" after the review stage in cases where the reviewer has declined. I think it is enough for archiving purposes to know the amount of requests and the names of the reviewers who accepted and did the review.</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" It should be possible to be invited multiple times. I suspect the case of being invited again and again is not a big problem out in the real world, but if we find that it is, we can consider recording the number of invites a user has declined and providing that info to the editor when they are making the invitation.</p>
<p dir="auto">I think that we should store the email address for review requests. Without any user interaction, the data is not storing any private information on what the user did in the system. It is just recording input from another user -- the editor. In this sense, it is the private information of the editor, not the reviewer.</p>
<p dir="auto">Storing the email address allows us to record a meaningful editorial history and display a sensible list of review requests for editors. If and when they become a user, we can recover that information as part of their own record of activity (we show stats on review requests accepted/declined/completed).</p>
<blockquote>

</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">This I can confirm again and as long as the managing editor  is legally bound by the publisher to obtain signatures they can create the users and this process can be outside the platform.</p>

class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Hello,</p>
<p dir="auto">I made a user flow that reflects the all the research, discussions and feedback received on this issue over the last few years along with some minor testing with a small user group at the Copenhagen Sprint. A big shout out to <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/withanage/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/withanage">@withanage</a>, <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/ajnyga/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/ajnyga">@ajnyga</a>, <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/bozana/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/bozana">@bozana</a>, <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/asmecher/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/asmecher">@asmecher</a>, <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/jardakotesovec/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/jardakotesovec">@jardakotesovec</a> and John for helping me fine tune the work further and make the process more GDPR compliant.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Summary of the requirement</strong></p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>In the “Users & Roles” section of the settings, we add a new “Invite user to take a role” action that can be used to invite any user to the journal OJS software based on an email address. The email sent will add the following:</li>
</ol>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Invitation request along with details of the role, starting date etc.</li>
<li>ORCiD verification details</li>
<li>GDPR compliance</li>
</ul>
<ol start="2" dir="auto">
<li>Reviewer can be added to OJS in two ways</li>
</ol>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><em>Through the review section of the submission:</em> Here the Journal Manager (JM henceforth) / Editor can click on “Add a reviewer” action and will see the following: Reviewers already associated with the Journal and added to OJS and send a review request to them, “Add a new user”- here the JM/Editor can invite a user via email to not only review the submission but also be an OJS user in reviewer capacity- and “Enroll an existing user” - here the JM/Editor can add the reviewer role to a user who already has other OJS roles along with sending an invitation to review the submission.</li>
<li><em>Through the “Users & Roles” section:</em> Here the JM/Editor can either add a new user to OJS as a reviewer or add a reviewer role to an existing OJS user. The user will then be shown in the existing reviewer section of “Add a reviewer” on a submission.</li>
</ul>
<ol start="3" dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto">Multiple hosted Journal OJS Installation: For Multiple Hosted Journals, Editors/ JMs cannot access information of users of one Journal to another. In spite of the journals being hosted on the same OJS instance, the user will have to go through the verification again to protect the information to be GDPR compliant. This is the same method followed by likes of Slack wherein even if the channel is hosted by the same company, the invitation process needs to be followed and accepted by the user. However, I as a user will not have to create a new account, I can use my existing OJS logins and verify and accept the role.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto">Other important considerations</p>
</li>
</ol>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Even if the user information is publicly available, the JM / editor cannot input the information without consent. This will be translated in the journey in a way where the editors can input the information but they wont be stored in the system. They are shown to the user as suggestions when they accept the invite and the user approves or changes it. Post which the information is stored in the system</li>
<li>Co-author reauthorization is required even if the user is an existing OJS user</li>
</ul>
<ol start="5" dir="auto">
<li>ORCiD Pre-requisite</li>
</ol>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Starting with 3.5.0, ORCiD Verification would not happen through a plugin. We're rewriting ORCiD support to be integrated into OJS rather than maintaining a plugin. The option to make ORCiD mandatory should be present as part of the 3.5.0 implementation; it shouldn't be necessary to write up a plugin to add the "make ORCiDs mandatory" checkbox.</li>
<li>If  the JM/System Administrator/Editor has marked ORCiD verification as mandatory, then the email invitation sent will highlight that the verification is mandatory. If it’s not enabled then the ORCiD mandatory message on the email will not be shown</li>
<li>Mandatory or not, when the user is redirected to the ORCiD website to verify they have an option to skip the step. Since we cannot customize the ORCiD verification screen to show skip or not, the email will be the vehicle for communication.</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto">Below are the user flows for inviting users to a role in OJS</h3>
<p dir="auto"><strong>A. Landing Page ( Settings > Users & Roles > Users)</strong></p>

<p dir="auto">How the roles table functions</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Selecting a role from the drop down is compulsory</li>
<li>The start date auto defaults to “today’s date” with an option for the Journal Manager to set a date in the future as well as past</li>
<li>End date is not a field the JM can fill. Once the JM clicks on “Remove Role” the end date defaults to that date.</li>
<li>Journal Masthead --> always auto defaults to appearing in the masthead with options of them not not certain roles which can be managed from the settings</li>
<li>Once the JM clicks on “Remove Role” then not only the user access is removed but they stop appearing in the masthead as well</li>
<li>Nothing can be toggled or changed once invitation is accepted by the user</li>
</ul>

dir="auto">Continuing from the previous comment, here are the workflows for editors inviting reviewers.</p>
<p dir="auto">As mentioned above the reviewer can be added to OJS in two ways<br>
<strong>- Through the review section of the submission:</strong> Here the Journal Manager (JM henceforth) / Editor can click on “Add a reviewer” action and will see the following: Reviewers already associated with the Journal and added to OJS and send a review request to them, “Add a new user”- here the JM/Editor can invite a user via email to not only review the submission but also be an OJS user in reviewer capacity- and “Enroll an existing user” - here the JM/Editor can add the reviewer role to a user who already has other OJS roles along with sending an invitation to review the submission.<br>
<strong>- Through the “Users & Roles” section:</strong> Here the JM/Editor can either add a new user to OJS as a reviewer or add a reviewer role to an existing OJS user. The user will then be shown in the existing reviewer section of “Add a reviewer” on a submission.</p>
